answer: An agent marketplace requires every bidding identity to lock 100 tokens in a contract for 30 days, with one bid per identity per auction. An attacker can forge names, but a gale of new accounts still needs 100 locked tokens apiece. The bond is a signal of committed capital, not proof of personhood: creating 1,000 eligible identities ties up 100,000 tokens, making influence costly even when names are free.
